title: Flow Boundary Harmonizer for Realtime Chat Batch Formation
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Problem: Streaming chat completions currently suffer intermittent token emission stalls and suboptimal GPU memory utilization when many short-turn conversations interleave with long-turn streams. Current continuous batchers either prioritize latency at the cost of increased KV duplication / GPU fragmentation, or aggregate aggressively and spike p95 latency. Goal: Design and ship a flow-boundary-aware batch formation heuristic that harmonizes three concerns: (1) keep streaming token latency stable, (2) minimize per-session KV duplication and redundant GPU allocations, (3) reduce peak GPU memory fragmentation using slab consolidation heuristics.
acceptance_criteria: P95 token emission latency for streaming chat <= 120ms under mixed workload (40% short-turn, 60% long-turn)
KV duplication per unique session reduced by >= 30% on average compared to baseline
Peak GPU memory usage reduced by >= 12% on standard 8xA100 serving cluster for the benchmark workload
No regression in tail error rate (5xx) and fallbacks remain within SLOs
Feature gated behind runtime feature-flag and rolloutable via Console with canary ratio control
tasks: Design: document heuristics and gating rules in Confluence (link: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RUNTIME/Flow+Boundary+Harmonizer)
Prototype: implement heuristic in the open batcher module (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/____ )
KV strategy: add anticipatory KV warmup + soft-prefetch policy and benchmark hit-rate improvement
GPU allocator: integrate a slab consolidation pass that coalesces small allocations at turn boundaries
Perf tests: create mixed-workload benchmark and runner in perf infra
Rollout: add feature-flag + metric dashboards and gradual ramp plan
Docs: update Console runbooks and SDK notes about new batching behavior
notes: Heuristic sketch: classify incoming requests into flow buckets by recent turn-length distribution and entropy estimate. Short-turn flows get low-latency microbatches with strict GPU slab reservation; long-turn flows are admitted into elastic bundles that tolerate slightly higher assembly delay but share KV slots aggressively.

KV management: use a 2-tier KV retention policy — hot-kept prefixes for short-turn flows (short TTL, high keep probability) and queued cold-shards for long-turn flows (longer TTL but evict-first on memory pressure). Add opportunistic prefix reuse by matching conversation embeddings hashed to bucket ids.

GPU memory: slab consolidation triggers at flow boundaries to pack surviving KV slices into contiguous slabs, reducing fragmentation. When consolidation runs, lock duration capped at 4ms to avoid adding jitter to stream emission. We accept a tiny scheduling jitter in exchange for lower long-term memory pressure.

Gating rules: if GPU free memory < 18% OR observed eviction rate > 1.2 evictions/sec per GPU, switch to aggressive consolidation + conservative bundling mode. Otherwise operate in latency-first mode for short-turn traffic.
Metric surface: token_emit_p95, kv_duplication_rate, gpu_peak_memory, kv_eviction_rate, batch_assembly_latency_p50/p95, slab_consolidation_runtime_ms

Trade-offs: anticipatory KV warmup increases transient memory, but reduces duplicate recomputation and improves latency stability. We counterbalance with faster consolidation and a conservative TTL policy to limit long-lived KV items.
